summary: Jiayao An specializes in sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Bai Su around 1979 to 1982 and held posts around 1982 at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, including its Institute of Archaeology.
Jien Abe was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who was a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He served as a professor at Meiji University until 2001.

Jifu Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tunghai University from around 1965 to 1969 and served as a full-time researcher at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies from around 1985 until retiring in 2019.

Jigdal Dagchen Sakya was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under traditional teachers Ngawang Thutop Wangchuk, Dzongsar Khyentse Chokyi Lodro, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and held a post at the University of Washington from circa 1960 to 1963.

Jigme Chhoeda is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Druk Sangag Choeling Monastery and Tango Monastery. He served as abbot at Tango Monastery (~1986) and held posts at Dratshang Lhentshog and the Central Monastic Body.
Jigme Tenpai Nyima studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Terton Sogyal, the latter of whom he also taught.
Jigmeth Junu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2013) under supervisor Yongdong Shi, having also studied under traditional teacher Hui Xian.
Jikai Fujiyoshi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a post as a member at Kyoto University (attested 1967) and served as a professor at Rissho University.

Jikido Takasaki was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from the University of Tokyo and Savitribai Phule Pune University. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Osaka University, Komazawa University, and Waseda University.

Jim G. Shaffer is an archaeologist and Indologist. He earned his B.A. from Arizona State University (~1961–1965), his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1966–1972), and served as professor of anthropology at Case Western Reserve University (~1975–2017).

Jim Rheingans, a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned degrees from the University of Hamburg, Bath Spa University, and University of the West of England. He holds posts attested in 2026 at the universities of Hamburg, Vienna, and Sydney.

Jin Kyoung Choi is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Munich and Ghent University. Attested in 2026, Choi held posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and Ghent University.

Jin Y. Park is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a visiting fellow at City University of Hong Kong and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy and Religion at American University (attested 2007–2012).
Jin-il Chung is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts as a staff member (attested 2008) and editor (attested 2026) at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Jinah Kim, a scholar of South Asian art, Indology, and Buddhist studies, earned her PhD at UC Berkeley (attested 2007). She held appointments at Vanderbilt University and the Institute for Advanced Study, and is a professor at Harvard University.
Jinchuan Wan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held posts as a professor at Fo Guang University and National Central University (both attested in 2010).
Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995) and served as Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010).

Jing-shen Tao is a sinologist and historian. He studied at National Taiwan University and Indiana University Bloomington (Ph.D. ~1964–1967), and he served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000).
Jingyi Yang works in computational fields, Indology, and Tibetology. Yang has studied at and served as a project staff member at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Jinhua Chen, a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, completed graduate studies at McMaster University and postdoctoral research at Kyoto University under Noritoshi Aramaki. He held positions at the University of Virginia and the University of British Columbia.
